name: Gas-fired steam and hot-water boilers
applications: process steam for refineries, petrochemical and industrial plants
on-site utility steam and combined heat and power
supplementary firing in HRSGs behind gas turbines
fuel-flexible CFB steam generation and solid-fuel-to-gas conversion
principle: A gas-fired boiler burns natural gas (or another gaseous fuel) in a contained furnace and transfers the heat through pressure-part surfaces to water, producing steam or hot water. Package fire-tube boilers pass hot gas through tubes surrounded by water; water-tube boilers pass water through tubes in the gas path and separate steam in a drum or use once-through circuits; condensing designs cool the flue gas below its dew point to recover latent heat. Low-NOx burners, flue-gas recirculation and post-combustion catalysts control emissions. Heat recovery steam generators raise steam from gas-turbine exhaust and may burn additional gas in the duct.

process_steps.name: Gas and combustion air are metered and conditioned
equipment: double block and bleed shutoff valves

process_steps.name: Low-NOx burner fires into the water-cooled furnace
Heat crosses the heat-transfer surfaces into boiler water
Steam separates and is conditioned for export or the turbine
Condensate and make-up are deaerated, heated and pumped back
Flue gas passes heat recovery and emission controls to the stack

key_equipment: burner management and flame safeguard system
fire tubes or water tubes and tube sheets
safety relief valves and blowdown system

performance.metric: minimum combustion efficiency, large gas-fired commercial hot-water boiler
performance.basis: US DOE FEMP purchasing requirement for 2.5-10 MMBtu/hr input gas-fired hot-water boilers, based on 10 CFR 431.86; federal purchase minimum, not a product rating.

performance.metric: AHRI thermal efficiency, condensing gas hot-water boiler
performance.basis: Cleaver-Brooks ClearFire-CE technical data: AHRI combustion 94.7%, AHRI thermal 96.0%; 'up to 99%' is OEM marketing wording and is not used here.

performance.metric: NOx, natural-gas low-NOx burner without FGR
performance.basis: Zeeco PLN brochure ladder: 40 ppm at 40% excess air, 30 at 45%, 15 at 50%, 9 at 60%; the page does not state the O2 reference basis, so these are not directly comparable to 3%-O2 figures.

performance.metric: NOx, natural-gas burner at about 3% O2 without FGR
performance.basis: Cleaver-Brooks SBR-30 under 30 ppm; John Zink ECOjet Edge+ as low as 15 ppm without FGR in select applications (vendor claims).

performance.metric: NOx, ultra-low-NOx burner with flue-gas recirculation
performance.basis: Cleaver-Brooks SBR-5 with induced FGR at about 3% O2 (body states 3-4%); ALZETA surface-stabilised burner below 5 ppm corrected to 3% O2.
Cleaver-Brooks SBR-30/SBR-5 and Zeeco PLN/GO stated firing turndown on gaseous fuel; ClearFire-CE condensing boiler also 10:1.

performance.metric: efficiency improvement per feedwater temperature rise
performance.basis: Spirax Sarco: in broad terms each 10 C increase in feedwater temperature gives about a 2% boiler efficiency improvement.

performance.metric: US combined-cycle capacity equipped with duct burners
performance.basis: About 75% of the 278 GW US combined-cycle fleet, EIA data from EIA-860 and EIA-923, article 15 June 2022.

reference_plants.name: Sultan Ibrahim power plant, Track 4A (Pasir Gudang, Johor)
reference_plants.capacity: 1,440 MW total; two 9HA.02 gas turbines, two once-through HRSGs

reference_plants.name: GS Caltex Yeosu complex (SOLEX burner retrofit)
reference_plants.capacity: 32 SOLEX burners; under 5 ppm NOx, SCR avoided

advantages: commercial, widely available technology with packaged delivery and short erection times
natural gas gives low particulate and sulphur emissions and straightforward control
modern low-NOx and condensing configurations reach very low NOx and high efficiency
fuel flexibility: dual-fuel, refinery gas, hydrogen blends and CFB gas conversion
limitations: NOx figures from different vendors use different O2 and excess-air bases and are not directly comparable
condensing operation needs corrosion-resistant heat-exchange surfaces and condensate management
gas supply pressure and composition must be managed; booster/compressor sizing was not evidenced in this sweep
HRSG and duct-burner scope at named combined-cycle plants is often not explicit in the cited pages
notes: Process provenance: sources read 2026-11-24 cover shell/water-tube construction (Spirax Sarco), burner and emissions performance (Cleaver-Brooks, Zeeco, John Zink, ALZETA, Miura), feedwater and safety practice (Spirax Sarco, B&W), HRSG duct firing (GE Vernova, EIA, Tetra, B&W), CFB gas conversion (Zeeco, EPA) and codes (ASME, NFPA 85, EPA Boiler MACT). Vendor performance claims are labelled as such; no figure was estimated.
